title: The Mouse Deer Steals Cucumbers
summary: A hungry mouse deer steals cucumbers from the Farmer's garden. But the Farmer is no less clever!
moral: Taking what belongs to others without permission is wrong. It is better to ask politely!
pages: The dry season came and lasted so long. The grass turned yellow and the fruit in the forest dried up. The mouse deer walked wearily, holding its stomach. 'I am so hungry...' it groaned.
From behind the bushes, the mouse deer's nose sniffed something fresh. At the edge of the village was the Farmer's cucumber garden, green and full of fruit. 'Hmm, so fresh!' it whispered, peeking.
The mouse deer slipped into the garden. Crunch, crunch! It devoured the fresh, crisp cucumbers. Day after day it came again, and the Farmer's garden grew more and more bare.
'Who is stealing my cucumbers?' the Farmer wondered, annoyed. He made a scarecrow, then smeared it with sticky jackfruit sap. 'Just you wait, little thief!' he said.

That night the moon shone. The mouse deer came again and saw a figure standing in the middle of the garden. 'Hey, move aside!' There was no answer. The mouse deer kicked, and splat! Its foot stuck. It kicked with the other foot, and that stuck too. The mouse deer was trapped!
In the morning, the Farmer found the mouse deer stuck to the scarecrow. 'Aha, caught you!' The mouse deer was put into a bamboo cage. It was sad and full of regret.
The mouse deer had an idea. It lay still and held its breath, pretending to be dead. 'Poor thing, it is dead,' said the Farmer, then opened the cage and threw it into the bushes.
As soon as the Farmer turned around, the mouse deer opened its eyes, jumped, and ran like the wind. 'Thank you, Farmer!' it called from afar. From then on the mouse deer never stole again. The end.
